title: ‘Venial from the event’: any sin that actually obtains pardon
source_text: II. Peccatum veniale ab eventu ipsis dicitur peccatum quodlibet, quod per poenitentiam expiatur, & actu veniam a Deo consequitur, quantumlibet alioqui in se grave & atrox fuerit. Adeoque peccata hoc sensu venialia non opponuntur absolute peccatis mortalibus; sed eis solum quae reipsa nunquam remittuntur; ac per hoc ad mortem perducunt aeternam.
pass_a_gloss: Sin venial from the event is said by them to be any sin whatsoever which is expiated by repentance and actually obtains pardon from God, however grave and atrocious it may otherwise have been in itself. And so sins venial in this sense are not opposed absolutely to mortal sins, but only to those which in reality are never remitted, and through this lead to eternal death.
pass_b_english: ‘Venial from the event’ means any sin that repentance actually clears and God pardons.
In that loose sense it is not set against mortal sin as such, but against sins that never are forgiven.

choices.why: Outcome-based acceptation, not degree of gravity.
